newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Emperor sees 145,000 oz Fiji gold find.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Emperor sees 145,000 oz Fiji gold find.

text.p: Emperor Mines Ltd said on Tuesday it had identified from drilling so far an inferred mineral resource of about 526,500 tonnes grading 8.6 grams per tonne (g/t) gold at its Tuvatu prospect in Fiji.
This would equal about 145,000 ounces of gold, Emperor said.
Emperor said the inferred resource was based on drilling to date which was at an early stage of a planned resource estimation programme.
The Tuvatu orebody is open at depth and along strike, it said.
Drilling has been suspended for the wet season but an extensive drilling programme has been planned and is expected to significantly increase the resource tonnage, Emperor said.
The resource identified so far was likely to be mined from a single open pit, it said.

At the operating Vatukoula gold project in Fiji, the eastern area of Matanagata has yielded some intersections in the last six months which have significantly increased the orebody's inferred resource, Emperor said.
The area between the Musunagata fault and Homeward Bound (being 600 metres on strike from 16 to 22 level) has now delineated an additional inferred mineral resource of 170,000 ounces, Emperor said.
This increased the overall Matanagata Mineral Resource to 2,005,000 tonnes grading 8.16 g/t.

"The Matanagata orebody, for the last four years, has been the single largest orebody source of ore for Emperor's Vatukoula, Fiji mine, producing in excess of 150,000 ounces from 450,000 tonnes at a grade of 10.6 g/t," it said.
The new resource will enable production from Matanagata to be extended by five years at high grade, Emperor said.
Turning to its R1 capital development programme at Vatukoula, Emperor said development of 14 level continued throughout the last quarter and three of the R1 orebodies were. intersected.
At the current rate of development, production from R1 will occur four months ahead of schedule, it said.
